title: Flight Controller Board
body: The satellite's main computer. It runs the flight software, talks to the ground through the radio, and decides which subsystems get power. In this model it is a simplified placeholder shape.

title: Battery Board
body: Holds the lithium-ion cells and the power electronics (EPS) that charge them from the solar panels and hand out regulated power. V3 and later boards carry their own RP2040 microcontroller.

title: Mass Block (Payload Slot)
body: TODO: Michael to confirm. A lead block that stands in for a payload, so the satellite has a realistic mass and centre of mass. A real mission would put its payload board here.

title: XY Solar Panel (X+)
body: One of four side panels. Its solar cells charge the battery, and its sensors (sun, temperature) and magnetorquer coil help the satellite know and change its orientation.

title: XY Solar Panel (X−)
body: One of four side panels. Its solar cells charge the battery, and its sensors (sun, temperature) and magnetorquer coil help the satellite know and change its orientation.

title: XY Solar Panel (Y+)
body: One of four side panels, identical to the others. TODO: Michael to confirm this face is Y+ (axis read from the Onshape export, not the flight frame).

title: XY Solar Panel (Y−)
body: One of four side panels, identical to the others. TODO: Michael to confirm this face is Y− (axis read from the Onshape export, not the flight frame).

title: Z− Solar Panel
body: The bottom face. Six small solar cells plus a temperature sensor, a light sensor and a haptic motor driver, wired to the stack over one 5-pin connector.

title: Antenna Board (Z+)
body: The top cap. It holds the folded antenna elements down until the satellite is in orbit, then releases them so they spring out. TODO: Michael to confirm release mechanism wording.

title: Antenna Elements
body: Two lengths of steel tape measure that form a dipole. Each is cut to about 165 mm for the 437 MHz amateur band. TODO: Michael to confirm these two bodies are the stowed elements.

title: 1U Structure (half A)
body: The frame is two identical sheet-metal halves bolted together. It sets the 10 cm cube shape that fits the deployer, and every board mounts to it.

title: 1U Structure (half B)
body: The second of the two identical frame halves. Splitting the frame in half makes it cheap to cut and easy to open for integration.

title: Feet
body: The corner feet are the only parts that touch the deployer rails. TODO: Michael to confirm which feet carry the deployment switches and the difference between the two foot styles.

title: Card Brackets
body: Small brackets with press-in nuts that tie the board stack to the frame. TODO: Michael to confirm.

title: Fasteners
body: M2.5 screws and nuts that hold the kit together. TODO: Michael to confirm what the "Combine1" and "Boss-Extrude1" bodies are.
